value.rationale: The centered fourth Lipschitz moment is a natural sharp L4 analogue of graph spread, measuring higher-tail concentration of Lipschitz observables on a standard distance-transitive graph family. The full formula and classification reveal an intrinsic optimizer phase change at 12 deleted matching pairs, different from the established L2 threshold of 8. This is not a mere recomputation of L2, as different moment orders select distinct extremizers and require a new quartic comparison. The structurally known vertex set limits originality and is acknowledged as a material risk.
